name: Axone Pork
subtitle: naga pork belly stewed to spoon-softness with fermented funk and raw chilli heat

ingredients.qty: 800g belly, skin on, cut into 3cm cubes

ingredients.note: axone, the fermented soybean cake this dish is named for, has no equivalent in the catalogue; dried fish gives the same fermented savoury backbone, though the aroma is different. If you can find axone, use 2 tbsp instead
for raja mircha, the Naga king chilli; two fresh bird's-eye chillies alongside gets you closer
not traditional everywhere, but common in Kohima kitchens
fresh or brined; rinse brined shoot twice

prepNotes: Use belly with a decent fat cap. Lean pork gives a thin, joyless version of this dish. The rendered fat is the cooking medium and there is no added oil.
Rinse the dried fish twice in warm water, pat it dry, and dry-roast it 3 minutes before it goes in.
Naga cooking uses no oil and almost no dry spice here. The flavour comes entirely from pork fat, ferment, ginger and chilli, so all four have to be good.

steps.text: Put the pork cubes in a heavy dry pot over medium heat with 2 tbsp of the water and cook 10 minutes, turning, until the fat has rendered and the cubes are browning in their own fat.
steps.tip: No oil goes into this pot at any stage. If it sticks in the first two minutes, add a spoon of water, not fat.

steps.text: Add the onion, garlic and half the ginger and fry 5 minutes in the rendered fat, until the onion has gone soft and translucent.
Stir in the torn dried chillies and the roasted dried fish and fry 2 minutes, until the whole pot smells sharp and savoury.
steps.tip: This is the moment the kitchen turns pungent. That smell mellowing into the pork over the next hour is the point of the dish.

steps.text: Add the tomato, if using, and cook 3 minutes until it breaks down.
Pour in the rest of the water, add salt, cover and simmer very gently 45 minutes. Check at 30 minutes and add a splash if it looks dry.
Add the bamboo shoot and the green chillies and simmer uncovered 10 minutes more.
The pork is ready when a piece of skin gives completely under a spoon and the gravy has reduced to a thick, glossy few centimetres in the base.
steps.tip: If it is still chewy, it needs time, not heat. Go another 15 minutes covered on low.

steps.text: Stir in the remaining ginger julienne and the spring onion, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and serve with plain sticky rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves overnight as the ferment settles into the fat. Lift off the set fat cap, reheat gently on the stovetop, and add fresh ginger and spring onion at the end.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
